hypothesis: Full-model continuations can improve aggregate precision while erasing supported rare-label behavior. A long-tail decoupled classifier retraining stage can keep the incumbent representation exactly frozen and adjust only Product-18 output rows under label-balanced sampling, improving label breadth without representation forgetting.
differenceFromClassBalancedV1: class-balanced-v1 updated the full model with positive-weighted BCE. This experiment freezes the encoder and classifier feature transform, uses ordinary BCE, and changes only Product-18 output rows through one class-balanced sampling stage.

featureAndSampling.features: deterministic incumbent eval-mode tanh(classifier.dense(CLS)); encoder and dense transform frozen
featureAndSampling.rowWeight: empty rows receive 1/empty_count; positive rows receive the maximum inverse combined-train positive count among their Product-18 labels

training.updatedParameters: only the 18 Product-18 rows and biases of classifier.out_proj; all other tensors remain incumbent values
training.loss: ordinary unweighted Product-18 BCE on sampled frozen features
training.checkpointSelection: single final head; no intermediate evaluation or sweep

inference: unchanged Product-18, global threshold 0.35, canonical max-two selector
